chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Union meetings and Pinky the drummer
summary: Musicians complained at Local 802 meetings that white players earned more, a fight led by drummer Pinky.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: I won't argue that point, a point well taken. But they never complained about things like that?
Yeah, they complained. Sometimes they had meetings. That's why they had meetings down at the Local 802. They brought the scale up and put things even.
What do you mean by put it even?
If you're a musician, you play, you deserve your money, you get the scale, you get your money, you call it a day. One as good as the other. If you can't make it, shame on you.
I don't understand. If you had a union and if the union is making scale, if the scale is set, why is it that there would be an argument as to one musician making more money than the other?
Well, why does the president make more than the secretary? He's the top man.
But this is for all, black and white.
You can't compare them together but somebody's more than somebody else.
But it wasn't a thing divided among race lines, that the black musicians were making less than the white musicians? That's the point I'm trying to say.
That's the way it started, when I came in.
They were complaining because the white musicians made more than the black musicians?
That's exactly what they did.
Who was leading - who started inciting all these people to think like this? Was it anybody in particular or everybody just felt that way?

I mentioned one but you don't know him. He's a drummer, very good drummer, name was Pinky ( ? ). That's when Local 802 was on Lexington Avenue because I went over there to join. They was fighting about who wanted to be who or whom. Fighting about the president and the secretary and he was fighting the president. We lived in the same building in the same street as Fletcher Henderson, Pinky Bujimi. He's a Negro drummer and a very good one too and would fight anybody anytime. He'd say, we're entitled to it just as much as you are. We play just as much.
What was the white argument. What did they say?
Oh, brother, take me about 20 years to tell you.
They just had every excuse under the sun, huh?
You know, they want to win. I'll put it like that. But the biggest majority of the time white people will win but they're not going to continue to win. I don't think so.
They win in that particular instance?
Any instance when it comes to music.
They just dominated the field.
